title: Normalized square-zero ideal and fibre-product stalk data
statement: Use the tensor product of module sheaves [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], normalized first-order thickening site models and chart ring maps [def-sfb-space-square-zero-extension-data], the canonical tensor pullback and local tensors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], and pointed stalk presentations [def-sfb-space-pointed-stalk-data]. For a thickening site model $T$ of $X\hookrightarrow X'$, put $R_T(U)=\Gamma(T^{-1}U,\mathcal O)$. A square-zero ideal presentation is an $\mathcal O_X$-module sheaf with a natural sectionwise injective additive inclusion into $R_T$, image the kernel of its quotient to $\mathcal O_X$, with square-zero products and quotient scalar action; require the quotient to be locally surjective. For a morphism of spaces and two pointed stalk presentations, a normalized stalk ring map is a ring map agreeing on every compatible pointed chart pair with the specified chart ring map. A fibre-product ideal presentation uses the actual sheaf fibre product [def-sfb-space-sheaf-fibre-product], an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], its canonical map from $X$, the regular-functions stalk on that fibre product, and the restriction from $B'$ prescribed on all compatible pointed charts; its ideal is the kernel of this restriction. These are normalized data, with no existence assertion.
